questions.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 14\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-9{x}_{2}+6{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -9 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}10 & -6 \\ -6 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ 6 & 10\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-12{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 6 & 0 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}5 & 8 \\ 8 & 14\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}14 & -8 \\ -8 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ Equivalently, it is the acute angle between $x$ and any non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ So, to make calculations easier, we can find the angle between the vectors

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,2\,{\text{proj}}_{S}x=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot 0+2\cdot 3}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{6}\sqrt{18}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{6},
$$

which is already an acute angle.

questions.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}9 & 5 \\ 5 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 \\ -5 & 9\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ Equivalently, it is the acute angle between $x$ and any non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ So, to make calculations easier, we can find the angle between the vectors

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,2\,{\text{proj}}_{S}x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{0\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 1+0\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1}\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{4},
$$

which is already an acute angle.

questions.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 6 & 27\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 18\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{18}[\begin{aligned}27 & -6 \\ -6 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 18\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ Equivalently, it is the acute angle between $x$ and any non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ So, to make calculations easier, we can find the angle between the vectors

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,2\,{\text{proj}}_{S}x=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{(-6)\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot 3+3\cdot 6}{\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{3}^{2}}\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{3}^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{27}{\sqrt{54}\sqrt{54}} \\  & =\frac{27}{54} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{\pi }{3},
$$

which is already an acute angle.
